rationale: A wins because it keeps the central fact mostly clean: "A 1,400-location chain makes Oatly the default non-dairy pour across the US Northeast" is precise enough for a real foodservice reporter to work with. B keeps inflating "default non-dairy option" into a broader dairy displacement story, especially "One coffee chain just made dairy optional. Dairy is taking notice." That is not a sharper angle; it is a correction waiting to happen.
gaps_in_A: "Oatly wins its biggest pour-volume deal" invents "biggest" and pour-volume sizing; the update only says a 1,400-location regional coffee chain.
"same quarter" is tighter than the supplied facts; the update gives last-quarter loss context plus current rollout and plant closure, not a confirmed same-quarter bundle.
The customer angle's "Facts it rests on" includes "no price change at retail," which is irrelevant to a foodservice default-pour story and does no reporting work.
gaps_in_B: "made oat milk the default, not the option" misstates the fact. Oatly became the default non-dairy option, not the default milk overall.
"a chain-wide default switch away from dairy" and "One coffee chain just made dairy optional" overclaim the operational change; dairy is not shown to be optional or displaced.
"Dairy is taking notice" invents incumbent reaction that is nowhere in the update.
"whether 'default non-dairy' is becoming a real foodservice standard" is a padded trend angle from one data point; its own proof section admits it needs outside examples before it exists.
